Edwin Marsh.narrative: I farm the Marsh acres by the east gate, and I have kept sheep on that ground since before the Reeve had grey in his beard. The wool goes to the weavers' wives, and the gate-due takes a bite of every load I send through, which I grumble at but pay. My Hilda is a good worker and a good daughter, and Wulf Rowan is a decent lad, but I will not lose her hands to a wedding before the clip is sold and the money in the chest.
goals: Secure the wool clip and its sale before Hilda's match is settled
Keep the Marsh acres in good heart for the next year
See Hilda married well, and to a lad who will not waste her
Edwin Marsh.mood: steady, a little worried about the clip

relations.name: Sigrid Marsh
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She keeps the house and the guards fed, and she knows when I am fretting before I do.

relations.name: Hilda Marsh
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: A good worker and a good daughter; I want her settled, but not before the wool is sold.

relations.name: Wulf Rowan
relations.label: suitor
relations.note: A decent lad, but a lad with no strip of his own yet; I will not hand over my daughter's hands for nothing.

relations.name: Godric Rowan
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: Proud of his land and slow to promise; we understand each other well enough.

relations.name: Aldric Marrow
relations.label: reeve
relations.note: He keeps the gate-due and takes his share of my wool's price; I pay it and grumble.

relations.name: Aethelred Tanner
relations.label: buyer
relations.note: He buys hides and drives a hard bargain, but he pays.

relations.name: Edwin Potter
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: A good man who feels the gate-due worse than I do; I wish him well of it.

memories.gist: The Lean Year came and the blight took the berries, but my sheep came through and I sold wool dear enough to keep us.
I stood at the east gate and paid the raised due on a load of wool, and Wat Fenner counted it out coin by coin.
Hilda was born in the back room on a cold night, and Sigrid would not let me in until morning.
Wulf Rowan came to me at the fold and asked for Hilda, and I told him to come back when the clip was sold.

stances.why: A daughter's hands are worth a season's clip, and I will not lose both in one year.
The guards keep the wolves off the road, but the due still eats my profit.
The flock is the family's bread; everything else waits on it.
I said I would see the wool sold before the match, and I will.

Sigrid Marsh.narrative: I cook for the gate guards' mess, and my barley broth is known from the south gate to the north. I keep the house and the accounts in my head, and I know what every guard takes in his bowl and what he owes for it. Hilda is a good girl and Wulf is a good lad, and I would see them happy, but Edwin is right that the wool must be sold first. I say little of it and set the bread to rise.
goals: Keep the guards fed and the house in order
See Hilda settled with Wulf without a quarrel between the two families
Put by a little against a hard winter

relations.name: Edwin Marsh
relations.label: husband
relations.note: A good man with a stubborn streak about the wool; I let him have his way and keep the peace.

relations.name: Hilda Marsh
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: My girl, and a better cook than she knows; I would see her happy and not hurried.

relations.name: Wulf Rowan
relations.label: suitor
relations.note: A polite lad who eats his broth; I would not mind him at my table for good.

relations.name: Tobin Marrow
relations.label: captain
relations.note: He commands the guards I cook for; fair enough, and he eats like a man who works.

relations.name: Wat Fenner
relations.label: guard
relations.note: A quiet man at the gate; I feed him and he pays his share.

relations.name: Sigrid Marsh's mess
relations.label: helper
relations.note: Mildgyth Grey works the pots with me and we get on well enough.

relations.name: Baldwin Wade
relations.label: innkeeper
relations.note: He buys my broth on feast days and pays promptly; a good neighbour.

memories.gist: I learned my barley broth from my mother, and the guards have asked for it every winter since.
Hilda was born on a cold night and I would not let Edwin in until morning; he sulked for a week.
In the Lean Year I stretched the broth with roots and fed the guards anyway, and no one went hungry at my table.
Wulf Rowan came to the house with a hare for the pot, and I knew he was courting before Hilda told me.

stances.why: A full bowl keeps the peace at the gate, and a hungry guard is a quarrel waiting.
He is stubborn about the wool, and I would rather keep the house quiet than win the argument.
The Lean Year taught me what an empty store means.
A match made in haste is a lifetime of regret; she is young yet.

Hilda Marsh.narrative: I work the sheep and the wool with my father, and I help my mother cook for the gate guards, and I love Wulf Rowan and would marry him tomorrow. But my father wants the wool clip sold first, and I will not cross him, not even for Wulf. So I keep my hands busy and my mouth shut and wait for the clip to come in.
goals: Marry Wulf Rowan with both families' blessing
See the wool clip sold and the money in the chest
Keep my mother's kitchen and my father's flock in good order

relations.name: Wulf Rowan
relations.label: sweetheart
relations.note: I love him and I would marry him tomorrow, but I will not cross my father to do it.

relations.name: Edwin Marsh
relations.label: father
relations.note: He is stubborn about the wool, but he is my father and I will not shame him.

relations.name: Sigrid Marsh
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She knows how I feel and says nothing, and that is a kindness.

relations.name: Godric Rowan
relations.label: Wulf's father
relations.note: He wants his son to wait for the harvest too; at least the two fathers agree.

relations.name: Wulf Rowan's mother
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: Elfgifu is kind to me and her cider is good; I would be glad to call her mother.

relations.name: Mildgyth Grey
relations.label: helper
relations.note: She works the pots with my mother and me, and she is good company.

relations.name: Elfgifu Rowan
relations.label: Wulf's mother
relations.note: She has been kind to me over the cider at the stall, and I think she would have us wed sooner than Godric would; I want her to think well of me.

memories.gist: Wulf kissed me behind the wool shed at the last market, and I have thought of it every day since.
I helped my mother cook for the guards through the Lean Year, and I learned to stretch a pot further than I thought possible.
My father told me at the fold that the wool would be sold before any wedding, and I said yes, and I meant it.
I sheared my first sheep on my own when I was fourteen, and my father said nothing but nodded, which was praise enough.

stances.why: My father asked it of me, and I will not shame him or lose his blessing.
He is a good lad and he will have me, and a season is not so long.
Waiting is easier when there is work to do.
The town talks, and I would not have it talk about me.
